unit_routes.description: A string is the legacy routing edge. A rich route is a learner-facing material option for one unit: it explains the lecture-specific angle and coverage but does not impose an order.

format.description: What kind of artifact this is, which governs how it is used. 'exam' (past papers) and 'solutions' (worked model answers) are deliberately separate from 'exercise': a past paper is spent once under timed conditions, and model solutions are read as writing samples rather than solved.

angle.description: One line: what this material does for this lecture that the other options on it do not. Written for this lecture, never copied from the global source record.

angle_detail.description: The long form of the same judgment, shown on hover: what the reader gets, what it assumes, and where it departs from the taught deck. Optional only because the 2026-08 backfill is incremental; a newly authored route writes it.

depth.description: How deep this route goes. 'unassessed' means no contextual evaluation has been written yet, so the depth is genuinely unknown — it is not a judgment of shallowness and must never be inferred by an operator (CLAUDE.md §4).

scope.description: How this route relates to current exam scope. 'unevaluated' is distinct from 'optional': optional means assessed and judged skippable, unevaluated means the source is routed here but nobody has ever assessed it — visibility debt, made visible so it can be chosen or dismissed deliberately, and repaid on use rather than in bulk (WORKFLOWS §6a).
